prompt_text: I need a personal injury attorney in Chicago after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
I can recommend several respected Chicago personal-injury firms you should call and why each might be a good fit. Tell me a little about the crash (how seriously you were hurt, whether a commercial vehicle was involved, whether the other driver was uninsured, etc.) and I’ll narrow the list further. Note: my knowledge is current through mid‑2024, so please verify contact details and recent changes on each firm’s website.

Top Chicago personal-injury firms to call (and why)

1. Corboy & Demetrio
- Why: Long-established plaintiff’s firm in Chicago with a strong trial record in serious car-accident, wrongful-death, and catastrophic-injury cases. Known for high-value verdicts and handling complex insurance/ liability fights.
- Good if: Significant injuries, death, or disputed liability.

2. Clifford Law Offices
- Why: Nationally recognized for catastrophic injury and fatality cases, heavy trial experience, large resources for investigation and expert witnesses.
- Good if: Catastrophic injuries, long-term disability, catastrophic medical bills.

3. Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard
- Why: Focused on personal injury and patient safety claims, strong reputation for aggressive negotiation and trial practice in auto-accident cases.
- Good if: Severe injuries and you want a firm that regularly litigates rather than only settling.

4. Levin & Perconti
- Why: Known for high-value settlements and verdicts in catastrophic and wrongful-death matters; experienced with trucking and commercial-vehicle cases.
- Good if: Trucking collisions or very serious injuries with complex liability issues.

5. Power Rogers (Power Rogers LLP)
- Why: Regional plaintiffs’ firm experienced in auto collisions and catastrophic injuries — good trial experience and client advocacy.
- Good if: Serious injury and you want hands-on trial counsel.

6. Simmons Hanly Conroy
- Why: Large national plaintiff’s firm with substantial resources and medical-legal networks; handles large, complex cases including car crashes with catastrophic outcomes.
- Good if: Cases requiring big investigative resources or multi-discipline experts.

7. Rosenfeld Injury Lawyers (Chicago office)
- Why: Specializes in car accidents, handles uninsured/underinsured motorist claims, and offers free consultations and case evaluations.
- Good if: You need support handling insurance company tactics, including UM/UIM claims.

Other options/resources
- Illinois Trial Lawyers Association and Chicago Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service — use these if you want vetted referrals by specialty and locality.
- Local boutique firms: there are many smaller Chicago plaintiff firms that do excellent work and may provide more personalized attention — worth interviewing.

What to ask when you call (these help you choose)
- Do you handle my type of case (auto accident, trucking, uninsured motorist, pedestrian)?
- How many similar cases have you taken to trial in the last 3–5 years?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney vs. paralegal)?
- Do you work on contingency? What is your fee and what costs might be deducted?
- Do you have experience with insurance companies involved in my case?
- Can you provide recent examples/verdicts/settlements of similar cases?
- What is the estimated timeline and what are likely next steps?

What to have ready for the call
- Date/time/location of crash, police report number (if any)
- Photos of vehicles, injuries, and scene
- Names/contact of other drivers, witnesses
- Your medical treatment records or hospitals visited
- Insurance information (your insurer and the other driver’s)
- Any communication you’ve had with insurers (recorded statements offered/given)

Immediate practical steps (important)
- See a doctor and follow treatment recommendations (medical records are critical).
- Preserve evidence: photos, damaged clothing, vehicle damage, dashcam, phone videos.
- Don’t sign releases or give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without speaking to a lawyer.
- Be mindful of Illinois’ statute of limitations (generally two years for personal injury) — consult a lawyer promptly.

If you want, tell me:
- Your ZIP code (so I can focus on neighborhood firms)
- How badly you were injured and whether a truck/commercial vehicle was involved
I’ll narrow the list to 2–3 firms best matched to your situation and suggest specific questions to ask each when you call.
